items.title: Gold shop supervisor pawns RM176,200 in gold bars for cryptocurrency, gets 16 months’ jail
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — A former gold shop supervisor who pawned three gold bars to trade in cryptocurrency was sentenced to 16 months' jail and three strokes of the cane by the Sessions Court today for criminal breach of trust. He is also set to be sentenced on a separate criminal breach of trust charge over a pawned gold chain in another Sessions Court. The charges state that Koh, entrusted with three 999 gold bars weighing 50 grammes and 100 grammes, all worth RM176,200, pawned them at a pawnshop for his personal use.

items.title: Batu Kawan's MKH Oil Palm offer closes at 79.58pct
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Batu Kawan Bhd's mandatory take-over offer for the remaining voting shares in MKH Oil Palm (East Kalimantan) Bhd has closed, with the offeror and parties acting in concert holding 79.58 per cent. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd, acting for offeror Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd and ultimate offeror Batu Kawan, said the offer closed at 5pm on Thursday. The mandatory offer stemmed from Batu Kawan's acquisition of a controlling stake in MKH Bhd, which also triggered the obligation to extend an offer for MKH Oil Palm shares.

items.title: Johor stray dog catcher suspended after video sparks backlash
items.summary: Johor Health and Environment Committee chairman Ling Tian Soon said the action was unacceptable. Ling said stray animal-catching operations would be monitored to ensure they were carried out professionally. Meanwhile, MPBP said in a statement that the incident involved an appointed stray animal management contractor.

items.title: [UPDATED] Najib's special officer arrives at Langgak Duta residence
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A special officer to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak was seen arriving at his Langgak Duta residence this evening, hours after he was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. "We miss Datuk Seri Najib's leadership. Earlier today, the Federal Territories Pardons Board announced that Najib, 73, had been granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine.

items.title: MCA thanks King over Najib’s pardon, pledges to uphold constitutional supremacy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — MCA has expressed its gratitude to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, for granting a conditional royal pardon to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak. In a statement today, MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong said that honouring the Pardons Board’s decision does not negate the courts' earlier conviction of Najib, just as respecting judicial verdicts does not diminish the King’s constitutional prerogative to grant clemency. “MCA expresses our utmost gratitude for the royal assent granted by His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, regarding the conditional pardon of Former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak,” Wee said.

items.title: Road closures in George Town for Tanjong Lantern Festival tomorrow
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Several roads around Lebuh Armenian, Lebuh Acheh and Lorong Lumut here will be temporarily closed tomorrow in conjunction with the Tanjong Lantern Festival. The affected roads are parts of Lebuh Armenian from Lebuh Acheh to Lebuh Cannon, Lebuh Acheh from Lebuh Cannon to Lebuh Carnarvon, and Lorong Lumut. MBPP said public cooperation and attention were appreciated to ensure the festival proceeds smoothly and safely.

items.title: MCA: Judicial, pardon processes separate under Constitution
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MCA believes that the judicial and pardon processes should be understood as two separate processes within the framework of the Federal Constitution. MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong said the party expressed its appreciation to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia for the royal pardon granted conditionally to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak. "MCA believes that the judicial process and the pardon process should be understood as two separate processes within the framework of the Federal Constitution.

items.title: High Court dismisses RM1m suit over chair-pulling incident involving girl with cerebral palsy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in 10 states until 5pm today. It said in a statement that the adverse weather is forecast to affect the whole of Kelantan and Perlis, as well as Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Baling, Sik, Padang Terap, Pokok Sena and Pendang in Kedah; and Hulu Perak in Perak. Similar weather conditions are also forecast in Besut and Setiu in Terengganu; Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub, Bentong, Pekan and Rompin in Pahang; Hulu Selangor, Gombak and Hulu Langat in Selangor; Jelebu, Seremban, Port Dickson, Kuala Pilah and Rembau in Negeri Sembilan; and Alor Gajah and Melaka Tengah in Melaka.

items.title: Najib’s house arrest: DAP leadership to decide party stance tomorrow, says Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — DAP will convene an emergency central executive committee (CEC) meeting tomorrow to decide its formal position in response to the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, party secretary-general Anthony Loke announced today. Loke noted that the long-term financial fallout remains severe, citing recent Finance Ministry data indicating that 1MDB obligations have saddled taxpayers with RM51.4 billion in liabilities, comprising RM42.5 billion already settled and RM8.9 billion in outstanding debt. Earlier today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim maintained that the pardon does not dilute the government’s resolve to combat graft and power abuse.

items.title: No sign of Najib leaving Kajang Prison as of 3.30pm
items.summary: KAJANG: There has been no sign of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak leaving Kajang Prison as of 3.30pm today. More than 20 media personnel remained outside the prison entrance, waiting for further developments. Najib, 73, is currently serving a reduced six-year prison sentence at Kajang Prison after the Pardons Board reduced his original 12-year sentence in February 2024.

items.title: [UPDATED]: DAP CEC to meet tomorrow over Najib's conditional house arrest
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: DAP will hold a central executive committee (CEC) meeting tomorrow to discuss and decide on the party's position and subsequent course of action. The meeting follows the decision allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. In a statement, DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke said the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) scandal was a major corruption scandal in the country's history and had affected Malaysia's image and public and investor confidence in government institutions.

items.title: Police tighten security in Negri Sembilan amid royal institution developments
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: Police have tightened security measures across Negri Sembilan following developments concerning the state's royal institution. Earlier, Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir attended Friday prayers at the mosque, accompanied by his two sons, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin and Tunku Zain Al-'Abidin. Meanwhile, security has also been stepped up at Wisma Negeri in Seremban, which houses the Negri Sembilan State Secretariat.

items.title: ‘Thank you’: Negeri Sembilan ruler Tuanku Muhriz receives memorandum of loyalty
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Sept 18 — Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir today received a memorandum expressing loyalty and support for him after performing Friday prayers at the Tuanku Munawir Royal Mosque here. Tuanku Muhriz was accompanied by his sons, Tunku Besar of Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-’Abidin. After the prayers, Tuanku Muhriz received the memorandum from Dr Mohd Aluwi Sari, head of the Secretariat for Loyalty and Support for the 11th Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan.

items.title: Shark kills swimmer off beach in Western Australia
items.summary: SYDNEY: A shark killed a man as he swam off a popular beach near Perth in Western Australia on Friday, police said. It was the fourth death from a shark attack in Australia this year. "It was reported a male swimmer had been bitten by a shark while swimming along the coast," a Western Australia state police spokeswoman said in a statement.

items.title: Malaysia proposes Asean Halal Council launch in September 2027
items.summary: JAKARTA: Malaysia has proposed the formal establishment and launch of the Asean Halal Council in the country in September 2027 as part of efforts to turn the idea of a regional halal council into a functioning institution, according to Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. Zahid, who is also chairman of the Halal Industry Development Council (MPIH), said the proposal had been submitted to the Asean Secretariat and would next be brought to the Asean Summit in Manila for endorsement. He also viewed the Asean Halal Council as an important building block towards the proposed World Halal Development Council, with the discussion to be taken further at the Malaysia International Halal Showcase (MIHAS) in Kuala Lumpur later this month.

items.title: Sunway Healthcare breaks ground on RM800mil Johor hospital
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Healthcare Group has begun construction of Sunway Medical Centre Iskandar Puteri, its first hospital in Johor, with an estimated capital expenditure of RM800 million. Sunway Group founder and chairman Tan Sri Jeffrey Cheah said Sunway has always believed in Johor's immense potential and that quality healthcare is essential to sustaining the state's growth. This is through the planned Sunway Fertility Centre at Sunway Citrine, targeted for completion in 2027, and the Sunway Ambulatory Care Centre near the Johor Bahru–Singapore RTS Link, targeted for completion in 2028.

items.title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warning for 10 states until 5pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain, and strong winds across 10 states until 5pm today. In a statement, the department said the adverse weather is forecast to affect the whole of Kelantan and Perlis, as well as Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Star, Baling, Sik, Padang Terap, Pokok Sena, and Pendang in Kedah, and Hulu Perak in Perak. Similar weather conditions are expected in Besut and Setiu in Terengganu; Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub, Bentong, Pekan, and Rompin in Pahang; Hulu Selangor, Gombak, and Hulu Langat in Selangor; Jelebu, Seremban, Port Dickson, Kuala Pilah, and Rembau in Negri Sembilan; and Alor Gajah and Melaka Tengah in Melaka.

items.title: PAS welcomes Najib house arrest, says he still has plenty to offer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — PAS today thanked His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, for granting former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak a conditional pardon, saying he could still contribute his ideas and experience to the country. PAS secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the party was grateful for the King’s decision allowing Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to the payment of a RM50 million fine. PAS also prayed that Najib would remain in good health while serving the remainder of his sentence at home.

items.title: [UPDATED] Three students killed in Philippine school shooting, including gunman
items.summary: MANILA: Three students were killed in a school shooting in the southern Philippines on Friday, including a 16-year-old suspected gunman who turned the gun on himself, provincial officials said. The incident follows two fatal gun incidents since June at schools in the Philippines, where school shootings were previously rare. "After lunch, he started shooting students.

items.title: Segamat records highest haze reading in Johor at 161, three others unhealthy
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Haze worsened across Johor today, with four of the state's eight air quality monitoring stations recording unhealthy readings, led by Segamat at 161. Fine particulate matter measuring 2.5 micrometres or less was recorded at all eight monitoring stations. The remaining four stations recorded moderate readings – Larkin (97), Pasir Gudang (84), Pengerang (78) and Kota Tinggi (69).

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz attends Friday prayers, receives memorandum of support
items.summary: KUALA PILAH: Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir attended Friday prayers at the Tuanku Munawir Royal Mosque in Seri Menanti today, making his first public appearance after returning from abroad. Tuanku Muhriz left at 2.10pm. Today's development comes amid attention over Tuanku Muhriz's position as Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan following a disputed proclamation.

items.title: Pas: Najib can continue contributing ideas, experience under house arrest [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak can continue contributing his ideas, views and experience to the country while serving the remainder of his sentence under house arrest, Pas said. Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the party also expressed its gratitude to Allah and conveyed its appreciation to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, for granting Najib a conditional pardon. Under the pardon, Najib will serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine.

items.title: Indonesian teen held after RM1.29mil Kluang drug stash house raided
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: An 18-year-old Indonesian teenager was arrested after police busted a drug stash house in Kluang, seizing 25.95kg of drugs worth about RM1.29 million. Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the house, which was rented without a tenancy agreement, was believed to have been used as a stash house by a drug trafficking syndicate. "Police seized 25.95kg of drugs estimated to be worth RM1.29 million.

items.title: Albert Tei fails in bid to move five corruption charges to High Court
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The High Court today dismissed businessman Albert Tei’s application to transfer five corruption charges against him from the Sessions Court to the High Court. Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin dismissed the application by Tei, whose real name is Tei Jiann Cheing, 37, on the grounds that the issues raised were not complex and could be adequately dealt with in the Sessions Court. “I do not agree with the applicant’s (Tei) application.

items.title: Two Malaysians arrested over 10kg cannabis seizure in Singapore
items.summary: In the course of the checks, ICA officers uncovered four bundles of vegetable matter believed to be controlled drugs underneath the motorcycle seat. Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB) officers were alerted and further checks uncovered six more bundles of vegetable matter believed to be controlled drugs in a black haversack on the motorcycle handlebar, ICA said in a statement. "Investigations are ongoing," said ICA.

items.title: Anwar: Najib house arrest does not weaken govt’s fight against corruption
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 18 — The conditional pardon allowing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest does not weaken the government’s resolve to fight corruption and power abuse, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said all corruption cases, including ongoing proceedings involving Najib, must continue in accordance with the law. Anwar said Malaysia must remain firm in tackling corruption, with public support needed to ensure misconduct or abuse of power for personal enrichment is not taken lightly.

items.title: TNB to bear RM120mil-RM150mil AFA charge differentials between Sept and Dec 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) says it will bear an additional cost of RM120 million to RM150 million between Sept and Dec 2026 in automatic fuel adjustment (AFA) surcharge foregone to more than eight million domestic users who use electricity between 600kWh and 800kWh. This comes as the government decided to increase the "safety quota" for domestic usage to 800kWh a month, which will not be charged with AFA surcharges, retail charge and service tax, from 600kWh a month. The decision to increase the safety quota comes following complaints by certain members of the public that their electricity bills had increased drastically.

items.title: Johan Setia records highest unhealthy API reading at 192
items.summary: Nilai, Negri Sembilan, recorded an API reading of 179, followed by Kuching, Sarawak, at 178. Putrajaya recorded 175, while Seri Manjung, Perak, recorded 173. Both Shah Alam and Samarahan recorded an API reading of 171, while Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded 169.

items.title: Almost 13,000 patients on organ transplant waiting list as of July
items.summary: The Health Ministry, through the National Transplant Centre (NTC), said 12,228 adults and 307 children were waiting for kidney transplants, followed by liver (16 patients), heart (14), lungs (three), and heart and lung (seven). "For heart and lung transplants, the waiting period ranges from four months to 3.8 years, based on data from the National Heart Institute (IJN)," it said in a statement. It said 235 organs were recovered from donors as of July, comprising kidneys, livers, hearts, lungs, corneas, bones, heart valves and skin.

items.title: Japan-Malaysia energy ties put under the spotlight
items.summary: The forum focused on strengthening the Japan-Malaysia energy and industrial corridor, developing Malaysia's future energy ecosystem and making energy security bankable through transition finance. Japanese ambassador to Malaysia Noriyuki Shikata said Japan's technology and capital were increasingly flowing into Malaysia across strategic sectors. "The global energy transition is reshaping economic competitiveness and investment priorities.

items.title: KYM ventures into healthcare with RM33.5mil Regen deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: KYM Holdings Bhd is proposing to acquire a 70 per cent stake in specialist healthcare provider Regen Healthcare Sdn Bhd for a maximum consideration of RM33.5 million, marking its entry into Malaysia's healthcare sector. The proposed acquisition will diversify KYM's principal activities to include healthcare and specialised medical services, reducing its reliance on manufacturing. Regen provides specialist healthcare services, primarily orthopaedic and ambulatory care and operates facilities.

items.title: Teen loses RM1 mil lawsuit over chair prank injuries
items.summary: The 14-year-old filed the suit together with her father, Wan Amey Shahril Wan Ab Rahman, 39, as the first and second plaintiffs, respectively. They named three teachers, Ilyana Sari Ridzuan, Suhaida Abdul Rahman and Aizam Naim Mohd Junid; headmistress Hamidah Shamsudin; the ministry and the government as the first to sixth defendants, respectively, alleging negligence that resulted in the girl's injuries. She said the plaintiffs still had to prove, on the balance of probabilities, that the teachers' negligence had caused the loss or injury.

items.title: Former jewellery supervisor jailed 16 months over RM176,200 gold theft
items.summary: Pix by Fathil Asri KUALA LUMPUR: A former jewellery store supervisor was sentenced to 16 months in jail and three strokes of the rotan after pleading guilty to three charges of criminal breach of trust involving RM176,200 worth of gold bars. Koh Mun Hoe, 33, had taken three gold bars weighing 250 grammes from his employer's vault, pawned them and invested the proceeds in cryptocurrency, suffering losses of about RM235,000. The store manager conducted a stock check on June 16 and discovered that three gold bars — one weighing 50 grammes and two weighing 100 grammes each — were missing from the vault.

items.title: Three held as police bust drug stash houses in Senai, seize pistol, RM51,000
items.summary: Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the suspects were detained in two raids at adjoining houses in Kampung Sepakat Baru, Kulai, at 6pm on Sept 11. In the first raid, police arrested two men, one believed to be the syndicate's drug dealer and the other his accomplice. "Police seized a Czech-made CZ pistol and 79 rounds of 9mm ammunition.

items.title: Media camp outside Najib's residence following conditional house arrest
items.summary: Earlier today, the Federal Territories Pardons Board said Najib had been granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine imposed in the SRC International case. Najib, 73, is currently serving a reduced six-year prison sentence at Kajang Prison after the Pardons Board reduced his original 12-year sentence in February 2024. The board also reduced the RM210 million fine imposed on him to RM50 million.

items.title: Anwar says constitutional process must be followed in Negri Sembilan
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has stressed the need for the Negri Sembilan government to adhere strictly to constitutional provisions and established procedures in dealing with the dispute over the position of the Yang di-Pertuan Besar. He said the removal of a ruler was not a trivial matter and that any action involving the institution of the monarchy must comply fully with the Constitution. His remarks came amid a dispute over an April 19 proclamation purporting to remove Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir as Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan.

items.title: Three men fined RM4,500 each for assisting unlicensed moneylender
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Three men were each fined RM4,500 by the magistrate's court today after pleading guilty to charges linked to unlicensed moneylending. The three — Kelvin Tee, 24, Ng Yong Siong, 25, and Gavin Kho, 24 — were charged under Section 29AA of the Moneylenders Act 1951 for assisting an unlicensed moneylender. They pleaded guilty to three separate charges before the court.

items.title: Phase 2 testing on track, ECRL opening by mid-December: MRL chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Testing and commissioning for the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) Phase 2 is progressing well, keeping the project on track for its targeted opening, Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) said. MRL chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak said the second phase of testing, covering the Kuantan Port City-Gombak section, was currently underway following the completion of testing between Kuantan and Kota Bharu. He said the comprehensive inspection train (CIT) had begun testing the Kuantan-Gombak section, and the results so far show positive outcomes.

items.title: Teen driving Mercedes charged over crash that killed four family members in Kluang
items.summary: KLUANG, Sept 18 — A 19-year-old student pursuing studies in Singapore was charged in the Magistrate’s Court here today with reckless and dangerous driving over a crash that killed four family members last June. Goh Yin Zun pleaded not guilty after the charge was read to him through an interpreter before Magistrate Norasidah A Rahman, Berita Harian reported. Deputy Public Prosecutor Nik Noratini Nik Azam initially proposed bail at RM20,000.

items.title: Press swarm Kajang Prison and Langgak Duta after Najib’s pardon news
items.summary: KAJANG, Sept 18 — Kajang Prison and the residence of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak have become focal points for local and international media following the announcement that he has been granted a conditional pardon by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today. As of 12.30 pm, there was no movement involving the former prime minister detected at the Kajang Prison entrance. Najib, 73, has been serving his prison sentence at Kajang Prison since Aug 23, 2022.

items.title: Zahid announces Umno donation drive to pay Najib’s RM50m fine following conditional pardon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Umno has launched a nationwide donation drive to assist former party president Datuk Seri Najib Razak in settling the RM50 million fine required under his conditional royal pardon, party president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced today. Zahid said the party, representing its entire leadership and grassroots membership, conveyed its profound gratitude to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, describing the royal decision as a moment of tremendous relief for Najib, his family, and party loyalists who had “never ceased to hold hope and offer prayers” for his release. He also called on party members to welcome the royal decision with humility, decorum, and strict adherence to legal norms.

items.title: AGC rejects Zamri Vinoth’s bid to review charge over statement at KL rally
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) has rejected a representation by independent preacher Zamri Vinoth regarding a charge of making a statement likely to cause public alarm in connection with a gathering held in front of a shopping complex in the capital. Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Farhana Mohamad Poad informed Magistrate Faezahnoor Hassan of the decision during proceedings today. Lawyer Nur Shafiqah Shafiyah Omar, representing Zamri, subsequently requested that the court fix dates for the trial.

items.title: Haze update: 35 areas now with ‘Unhealthy’ API, Selangor’s Johan Setia tops 193
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Air quality across Malaysia deteriorated further by midday today, with 35 monitoring stations recording “Unhealthy” Air Pollutant Index (API) levels as of 12pm, according to Department of Environment (DoE) data. Selangor followed closely with six stations recording elevated pollution. Alongside Johan Setia, unhealthy levels were logged in Shah Alam (172), Banting (166), Petaling Jaya (165), Klang (160), and Kuala Selangor (139).

items.title: Hannah Yeoh denies signing Najib house arrest order, calls document fake
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh has denied signing any house arrest order involving former Prime Minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, which has been circulating on social media. Hannah made the statement in a post on her X account early today. “I have never signed any house arrest order as claimed in the document.

items.title: Najib gets conditional pardon, to serve remainder of sentence under house arrest
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 18 — Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has been granted a conditional royal pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest, the Legal Affairs Division announced today. “His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia has consented to grant a conditional pardon to Datuk Seri Najib Razak, allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until 23 August 2028, subject to his payment of a fine of RM50 million,” the statement said. The secretariat noted that Najib must strictly comply with all statutory terms attached to the royal pardon.

items.title: Malaysian Armed Forces plans special-needs child centres at major military camps
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) aims to establish at least one Community Rehabilitation Centre (PPDK) at major camps to care for children with special needs. Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the move is part of MAF's efforts to support its personnel, particularly those caring for special needs children. Meanwhile, Malek Razak said MAF is carrying out 898 maintenance projects involving 15,024 units of Armed Forces Family Housing (RKAT) to ensure comfortable living conditions for security force personnel.

items.title: Porsche driver surrenders after driving against traffic to flee Iskandar Puteri roadblock
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 18 — A 43-year-old local man has surrendered to the police after a viral video captured a white Porsche being driven against the flow of traffic to bypass a roadblock in Iskandar Puteri, Johor. In a statement on Thursday, Iskandar Puteri acting police chief Supt Saifullah Jaya @ Yahaya said the district Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division detected the 12-second clip circulating on social media, which showed the sports car being driven recklessly through a police checkpoint at KM6.5 of Jalan Ismail Sultan. The driver turned himself in at the Iskandar Puteri District Police Headquarters on the same day the footage surfaced.

items.title: Officials depart as FT Pardons Board meeting concludes at Istana Negara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Vehicles carrying Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh and former Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain were seen departing Istana Negara around 9.40am today following the conclusion of the Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting. The impromptu meeting has intensified public speculation that the board convened specifically to deliberate on the royal pardon petition of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, which was deferred during the board's previous sitting on September 11. During that earlier meeting, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, who chairs the board, granted royal pardons to 65 other inmates while Najib's case was held back for further consideration.

items.title: Total standstill on NSE northbound after two box vans overturn near Kuala Kangsar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — A crash involving two box vans that overturned on their sides has completely blocked all northbound lanes of the North-South Expressway (NSE) at KM257.7, along the stretch between the Menora Tunnel and Kuala Kangsar in Perak. The Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) reported that northbound traffic ground to a complete standstill following the incident, triggering a 1.7km congestion queue as of 9.18am. Emergency response teams and recovery machinery are currently on-site working to clear the obstructed lanes.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan’s Yang di-Pertuan Besar greeted by supporters at KLIA
items.summary: SEPANG, Sept 18 — Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir expressed his appreciation for the support shown by over 200 members of non-governmental organisations (NGOs) who gathered at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 here last night to welcome his arrival. Asked if he would immediately resolve the Negeri Sembilan royal institution impasse, Tuanku Muhriz replied briefly: “Yes, insya-Allah , insya-Allah . More than 200 members of Negeri Sembilan non-governmental organisations gather to welcome Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 1 in Sepang on September 17, 2026.

items.title: Police detain Chinese national after alleged theft attempt on Jakarta-Penang flight
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 18 — Police detained a Chinese national on suspicion of attempting to steal a passenger’s wallet during a flight from Jakarta, Indonesia, to Penang yesterday. Southwest district police chief ACP Anuwal Ab Wahab said police arrested the 55-year-old man at Penang International Airport after receiving a report from a 36-year-old Indonesian man about the incident. “During the flight, the Indonesian man saw the suspect remove his bag from the overhead compartment, open it and take his wallet.

items.title: Police sends probe papers on Umno delegate’s priest-nun comment to AGC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Police will submit the investigation papers on Selangor delegate Datuk Noorazli Said’s speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly on Sunday to the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) today. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M Kumar said the case is classified under Section 298 of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998. According to him, police received 86 reports and recorded statements from 93 witnesses, including members of the public, organisers, Umno delegates and Noorazli.

items.title: Weak 3.7-magnitude earthquake strikes off Sandakan, no tsunami threat to Malaysia
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 18 — A weak earthquake measuring 3.7 on the Richter scale was detected about 88 kilometres north of Sandakan, Sabah at 10.30pm yesterday. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a statement on Facebook, said the earthquake occurred at coordinates 6.6 degrees North and 118.3 degrees East. It said the epicentre was about 354 kilometres south of Palawan, Philippines and 88 kilometres north of Sandakan, at a depth of 392 kilometres.

items.title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warning for northern states, Sabah and Sarawak until noon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning covering multiple states across the country, cautioning that thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected until 12 noon today. In the northern peninsula, the entire state of Perlis is under warning, along with several districts in Kedah, including Bandar Baharu, Kulim, Pendang, Pokok Sena, Langkawi, Kubang Pasu, Kota Setar, Kuala Muda, Yan and Baling. Penang is also affected in its entirety, while Perak faces widespread impact across Hulu Perak, Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Hilir Perak, Perak Tengah and Kuala Kangsar.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan State Secretary’s Office backs AGC view, says won’t gazette April 19 proclamation on Ruler
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Sept 18 — The Negeri Sembilan government will not take any action to gazette or enforce the April 19, 2026 proclamation regarding the position of the Yang Dipertuan Besar, the Negeri Sembilan State Secretary’s (SUK) office said in a statement last night. It said the state government abided by the AGC’s view that members of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (MMKN) had no jurisdiction, authority, or power under the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 to announce the proclamation. Meanwhile, the Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) reiterated that Tuanku Muhriz remained the legitimate Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan and chairman of the DKU.

items.title: Passenger dies after medical emergency on Malaysia Airlines flight to Sydney
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — A passenger died on board a Sydney-bound Malaysia Airlines flight after suffering a critical medical emergency mid-air on Wednesday. Malaysia Airlines confirmed that the passenger on board flight MH141 from Kuala Lumpur to Sydney could not be revived despite immediate emergency medical intervention by crew members and qualified medical personnel on board, news.com.au reported. The flight departed Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday morning and touched down at Sydney Airport at 7.43pm local time.

items.title: New-generation MyKad drops Touch ’n Go feature, focuses on security, says NRD
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — The new-generation MyKad, which started being issued yesterday, no longer comes with the Touch ’n Go facility. In a social media post, the National Registration Department (NRD) said users can still access the service through the Touch ’n Go eWallet or a separate Touch ’n Go card. “For users who wish to continue using Touch ’n Go services, the facility can be accessed through the Touch ’n Go eWallet or a separate Touch ’n Go card,” it said.

items.title: FT Pardons Board convenes at Istana Negara amid talk of Najib’s petition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 17 — Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh and Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar have both reached Istana Negara here for a suddenly-scheduled Pardons Board meeting this morning. The meeting is shrouded by speculation that the board is being reconvened to determined pardon application of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, which had been deferred during the previous meeting on Sept 11. Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison, along with a RM210 million fine.

items.title: Sarawak and Selangor bear the brunt as 34 stations log ‘Unhealthy’ API levels in Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 18 — Air quality across Malaysia deteriorated significantly this morning, with 34 monitoring stations nationwide recording “Unhealthy” Air Pollutant Index (API) levels as of 8.30am, according to Department of Environment (DoE) data. Sarawak and Selangor hardest hit Sarawak emerged as the most affected state overall, with eight monitoring stations entering the unhealthy range. Selangor recorded the highest concentration of polluted areas in Peninsular Malaysia, with six stations logging unhealthy air quality.

items.title: Ice, fans and cooling pads: How Malaysia’s chicken farmers are beating El Niño heat
items.summary: Heat poses a far more serious challenge, and one that farmers cannot simply keep outside the door. A prolonged spell of extreme heat could affect how quickly chickens grow, how much farmers lose and how well they perform. Keeping the heat out Malay Mail recently visited Muzamri’s farm, where the broiler farmer and chairman of the Selangor Poultry Farmers Association has spent 26 years raising chickens.
